steps.name: Prepare ranked and significant gene lists from DESeq2 results
steps.context: Input is /data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, a DESeq2 results table (gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2fc SE/stat, p-value, padj) for the 6 lesional vs 6 control psoriasis skin contrast (12000 x 8). Use the actual column names present in the file (inspect header first) rather than assuming exact names.
steps.question: From de_results.csv (12000 genes, DESeq2 treated-vs-control contrast for psoriasis lesional vs control skin), what is the full ranked gene list (by signed statistic) and the FDR<0.05 significant gene set needed to run hallmark enrichment?
constraints: Do not re-run DESeq2 or touch the raw counts/metadata — DE is already done and this step only consumes de_results.csv
Use a signed ranking metric consistent with GSEA convention (e.g. sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue), or the DESeq2 Wald/stat column if present and preferred)
Gene symbols must be de-duplicated deterministically before writing the ranked list, since GSEA tools require unique identifiers
acceptance_criteria: Output is a ranked gene list (gene symbol -> ranking metric) covering all genes in de_results.csv with a non-missing p-value and log2 fold change, with duplicate/ambiguous symbols resolved (e.g. keep the row with the largest |ranking metric| per symbol)
A separate significant gene table (padj/FDR < 0.05) is produced, reporting up- and down-regulated counts separately
Reports how many of the 12000 gene rows were dropped due to missing values or symbol mapping issues

steps.name: Pre-ranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
steps.context: Use the MSigDB human Hallmark gene set collection confirmed present in the reference store (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC gene symbols, GMT format) — resolve its current path via the reference store rather than assuming a fixed path. Organism is human (taxon 9606), matching the gene symbols in de_results.csv.
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets are significantly enriched (positive or negative NES) between psoriasis lesional and control skin, using the full ranked DESeq2 gene list?
constraints: Confirm the Hallmark GMT reference is present before running; if absent, report the gap rather than substituting a different gene set collection
Use gene permutation or the standard prerank permutation approach with at least 1000 permutations for stable p-values
Report the fraction of ranked genes that matched Hallmark gene symbols, since incomplete symbol overlap changes the effective set sizes
acceptance_criteria: GSEA (prerank) is run against all 50 Hallmark sets using the ranked list from T1S1
Output table has one row per hallmark set with NES, enrichment p-value, and BH-adjusted FDR, sorted by FDR then |NES|
Sets with FDR < 0.25 (standard GSEA threshold) or FDR < 0.05 are explicitly flagged as significant, with direction (up in lesional vs up in control) stated per set

steps.name: Over-representation test of significant DE genes against Hallmark sets
steps.context: Uses the same MSigDB human Hallmark GMT reference as T2S1. The background/universe for the hypergeometric test must be the full set of ~12000 genes tested in de_results.csv, not a genome-wide default, to avoid inflated significance.
steps.question: Among genes significantly changed (FDR<0.05) between psoriasis lesional and control skin, which Hallmark pathways are over-represented, and do these calls agree with the prerank GSEA result?
constraints: Background universe must be restricted to genes actually present in de_results.csv, not all annotated human genes
Run up- and down-regulated significant genes as two separate ORA tests so direction is not lost
acceptance_criteria: Fisher's exact / hypergeometric ORA run separately for up-regulated and down-regulated significant gene sets against all 50 Hallmark sets, using all genes in de_results.csv as the background universe
Output table has odds ratio, p-value and BH-adjusted FDR per hallmark set per direction
A concordance summary is produced comparing ORA-significant hallmark sets against the GSEA-significant sets from T2S1, flagging any hallmark called significant by one method but not the other

steps.name: Synthesize hallmark pathway results and visualize
steps.context: Final integration step consuming the GSEA prerank table (T2S1) and the ORA table (T2S2) for the psoriasis lesional vs control hallmark enrichment analysis.
steps.question: What is the consolidated, ranked answer to which hallmark pathways change between psoriasis lesional and control skin, combining prerank GSEA and ORA evidence?
constraints: Do not present ORA-only or GSEA-only hits as consensus findings — label method-specific hits clearly
State plainly that this is a 12-gene bulk RNA-seq study (6 vs 6) and enrichment results should be read as hypothesis-generating, not as validated pathway activity
acceptance_criteria: A single merged table listing all 50 hallmark sets with GSEA NES/FDR and ORA odds-ratio/FDR (up and down) side by side, sorted by GSEA FDR
A dot plot or bar plot of the top significant hallmark pathways by NES (both directions) is produced

A short written summary lists the pathways significant by both methods versus only one, and explicitly notes the sample_01 low-library-size caveat as a residual noise source in the underlying DE table

plan.title: Hallmark pathway enrichment in psoriasis lesional vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: DE (DESeq2, 6 lesional vs 6 control) is already complete; the results table (de_results.csv, 12000 genes) provides log2FC, p-value and adjusted p-value per gene. The research question is purely about which hallmark biological processes shift between lesional and control skin, so no re-analysis of counts is needed. The plan runs a single enrichment track: (1) load and QC the DESeq2 results table, build a ranking metric (signed -log10(p) x sign(log2FC), or the DESeq2 stat column if present) for every gene with a valid symbol, and also derive an FDR<0.05 significant gene list for a complementary over-representation check; (2) run pre-ranked GSEA against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene set collection (50 sets, confirmed present in refs) using the full ranked list, which is the standard approach recommended when a full DE table (not just a significant subset) is available and avoids arbitrary cutoff-driven bias; (3) run a hypergeometric/Fisher over-representation test on the significant gene subset against the same Hallmark sets as a sanity-check/cross-validation of the GSEA result; (4) synthesize both into one ranked table of hallmark pathways with NES, p-value, adjusted p-value (GSEA) and odds ratio/adjusted p-value (ORA), flagging concordant vs discordant calls, plus summary plots (dot plot / barplot of top hallmarks by NES and by -log10 FDR). The library size caveat on sample_01 (~4x below median) is a DE-stage concern already baked into the delivered DESeq2 table and cannot be revisited here since raw counts are not being re-modeled in this plan; it is flagged in the interpretation as a residual source of noise particularly for lowly-expressed genes.
